about: Cullet's 64 residents on the first morning (docs/SMALL_CITY.md section 3), the anchors the drafted sheets must honour. Hand-written; checked by `living/tools/author_world.py cullet --check`. Each member: `occupation` is Cullet's trade key, `trade` its words; `wants` and `going_on` are section 3's anchors (private to the person's own sheet); `kin` names each relative and what they are to this person; `rhythm` is the starting day (wakes, sleep_h, works as [from, to] hours past midnight, past 24 for after midnight, an optional second_sleep as [from, to], work_at and evening as `lot:<plan id>` places or resource kinds, and a note); the compile turns it into the seed's `rhythm` (rises, sleeps, evening_hours, works as one span, second_sleep); `secret` is known only to the people `secrets` lists.

prompt.dead: The dead (the fever winter's nine, Sander Vane and the others the bible names) may appear in memories and stances but never in relations.
prompt.memories: (the fever winter six years ago, last autumn's storm, a melt that came out wrong, a catch, a game of counters, a wedding, the first day at the Cone or the weirs; the elders remember their parents' stories of the lean years, and nobody remembers the ships)
prompt.money: Money is drops, small glass tokens (the item `mark`), worth about a smoked fish each.
extra: Each member below has `wants` and `going_on`: the anchors of their sheet. The sheet must agree with them. They are that person's own; the others in the house know only what their own lines and the situations say.
A tie marked SECRET, a member's secret, and a secret situation are known only to the people they are listed under. Write every other member as not knowing them, even in the same house.
Each member has a usual day (rhythm): when they wake and sleep, when and where they work, where they spend their evenings. Write a life that fits it, as a habit they chose and can change, not a rule.
Nobody's sheet says what will happen. No plans of events, no outcomes: what each person wants, fears, believes and remembers on the first morning.

settlements.name: Cullet
settlements.character: a glassmakers' harbour on a treeless island: it burns kelp to ash, melts ash and sand into glass at the Cone, and grows its food under that glass; fish from the jetties and weirs, roots from walled plots, peat from the moor and one small wood
settlements.ledger: The custom of the Counting House: whatever goes into or out of the Store is told here and written. A debt written in the ledger is a public thing. Losses at counters that cannot be paid are written. Drops are cast only when the tally keeper asks the Glassmaster, and every casting is written.

ties: son of Nan Fenwick and Hobb Fenwick
brother of Posy Fenwick
follows Benedikt Orme and Sabine Quill about the Readers' House

members.name: Posy Fenwick
members.role: Nan and Hobb's daughter; one of the cullet yard children
members.wants: To be in Edda's band.
members.going_on: Plays in the cullet yard with Edda Hollin's band and Tilly Dunlin.
ties: daughter of Nan Fenwick and Hobb Fenwick
sister of Alder Fenwick
friend of Tilly Dunlin

households.house: the turf house on the Moss

members.name: Tam Roon
members.role: peat cutter; lives in the turf house on the Moss and sells peat to the Cone and the town
members.wants: To be paid more for peat.
members.going_on: Lives up on the moor. Comes down at 15:00 and stays at the Marver too long.
ties: husband of Eilidh Roon
father of Col Roon
sells peat to Vessa Pontil for the Cone and says she pays too little
drinks at the Marver with Halvard Dunmore and the Strand men

members.name: Eilidh Roon
members.role: peat cutter on the Moss; Tam's wife
members.wants: To move into town.
members.going_on: Cuts peat on the Moss and walks home to the turf house each evening while Tam stays at the Marver.
ties: wife of Tam Roon
mother of Col Roon
has looked at the empty houses in the Rows
knows how little peat the Moss gives against what the Cone burns

members.name: Col Roon
members.role: peat cutter on the Moss; Tam and Eilidh's son
members.wants: To know other people his age.
members.going_on: Walks the strand alone every evening.
ties: son of Tam Roon and Eilidh Roon
cuts peat with his parents and has never been to lessons
sees Lark Morrow on the strand and has not spoken to her

members.name: Marit Sedge
members.role: warden of the Hanger, the island's only wood, which she planted with her mother thirty years ago; lives alone in the Hanger cottage
members.wants: The Hanger standing.
members.going_on: Planted half the Hanger with her mother. Will not let anyone fell a tree, for a ship or for the furnace.
ties: has refused Bram Calloway his fourteen trees
has refused Vessa Pontil wood for the Cone
gave Jory Greave the seed of his fruit tree
lets the children gather fallen branches if they ask

households.house: the lamp house on the mole

members.name: Anselm Faro
members.role: keeper of the Watchglass: lights it at dusk and tends it till dawn, under the keepers' vow; has never missed a night in forty years
members.wants: The light kept, every night.
members.going_on: Lights the Watchglass at dusk and tends it till dawn. Sleeps 06:00 to 13:00. Has never missed a night.
ties: uncle of Livia Faro, whom he raised in the lamp house
swore the keepers' vow forty years ago
plays counters with Pieter Achterberg at dawn, when both are finishing
Rafe Dunlin fishes by his light
is paid for the oil by Aldous Quill's ledger

members.name: Livia Faro
members.role: renders lamp oil from fish at the lamp house, by day; Anselm's niece
members.wants: To know who the light is for.
members.going_on: Works by day. Has begun to wonder who the light is for.
ties: niece of Anselm Faro
buys fish for oil from Magda Tarn's catch
talks with Lark Morrow at the mole at dusk

members.name: Dolly Achterberg
members.role: keeps the Marver, the cookshop on Mid Row, eleven till ten; the Achterbergs live over it
members.wants: A full house every night, and gets it.
members.going_on: Keeps the Marver. Owes Petra Tarn twelve drops for smoked fish and says it is paid in meals. Lorcan Vane owes her.
ties: wife of Pieter Achterberg
mother of Roos Achterberg
owes Petra Tarn for smoked fish, and says the Tarns have eaten it off at her tables
Lorcan Vane owes her for meals and drink
SECRET: has taken six drops from Davin Vane against Lorcan Vane's debt, and Lorcan does not know

members.name: Pieter Achterberg
members.role: lights the Batch, the common oven, at three each morning
members.wants: The Batch hot for everyone who comes.
members.going_on: Lights the Batch at 03:00. Asleep by 13:00. Plays counters with Anselm at dawn, when both are finishing.
ties: husband of Dolly Achterberg
father of Roos Achterberg
plays counters with Anselm Faro at dawn
asks everyone who bakes at the Batch for a little peat

rhythm.note: Two sleeps, as the owner read his hours (2026-11-11): 22:00-02:30 and a long one from 13:00 to 19:00 after the Batch cools.

members.name: Roos Achterberg
members.role: serves at the Marver; carved the town's best counters and runs the nightly game under the arcade
members.wants: To beat Aldous Quill at counters, once.
members.going_on: Carves the counters and runs the nightly game.
ties: daughter of Dolly Achterberg and Pieter Achterberg
has never beaten Aldous Quill at counters
wins drops from Lorcan Vane most nights
friend of Neve Calloway

members.name: Benedikt Orme
members.role: the reader: keeps the ship-day tablets, teaches the children nine till twelve, and spends his afternoons at the Lintel
members.wants: To know what the Lintel is.
members.going_on: Teaches the children 09:00 to 12:00. Spends his afternoons at the Lintel with tablets.
ties: teacher of Sabine Quill, his pupil in the formal script
teaches the town's children, among them Alder Fenwick, who wants to be a reader
keeps the list of the graves on the Crown
has heard Otto Brandt ask about the clay under the Crown

members.name: Gwil Stannard
members.role: the only mason and roofer; patches roofs with slates from the roofless shells
members.wants: Every roof dry, and his favours paid.
members.going_on: Every roof leaks and he is one man. Owes favours all over town.
ties: husband of Cora Stannard
owes favours to Dolly Achterberg, Magda Tarn and Vessa Pontil, and is owed by half the town
takes slates from the shell of Mid Row 3
mended the Cone's cracked band with Corvin Hollin

members.name: Cora Stannard
members.role: grower on the Ladder; grows flowers in a corner of glasshouse 4
members.wants: Her flowers.
members.going_on: Grows flowers in a corner of glasshouse 4. Oswin wants the corner back.
ties: wife of Gwil Stannard
grows flowers in a corner of glasshouse 4 that Oswin Greave wants back
brings flowers to the graves on the Crown

secrets.text: Vessa Pontil is losing her sight and can no longer judge the colour of a melt. Runa only suspects it.
Aldous Quill wrote his own household's twenty-drop peat debt from the fever winter as paid. It was not paid.
markers: wrote it in the ledger as paid

secrets.text: Davin Vane has paid six drops of his brother Lorcan's debt to the Marver without telling him.
Ysolde Calloway does not want to sail on the Second Thought.
Tobiah Dunmore wants to fish, not stoke.

situations.summary: The peat barn and the Store hold about twelve days of the Cone at full fire. The Roons cut less than the town burns, about seven loads for every ten. The only other fuel is the Hanger's wood, which Marit Sedge will not let anyone cut.

sides.Vessa Pontil: The Cone must not go out. She buys the Roons' peat and has asked Marit for wood once and been refused.
sides.Tam Roon: The Cone cannot run without his peat and Vessa pays too little for it.
sides.Eilidh Roon: She knows better than anyone how little the Moss gives against what the Cone burns.
sides.Marit Sedge: Every tree cut is thirty years. She has refused wood for the Cone and for the ship.
sides.Bram Calloway: His ship needs fourteen of the trees the Cone also wants.

situations.summary: Vessa Pontil is sixty-one and has named nobody to follow her as Glassmaster. There are two blowers, Corvin Hollin and Imre Sarro. The last two Glassmasters named their successors; nothing says it must be so.

sides.Vessa Pontil: She means to choose, and soon, and has told no one whom.
sides.Ode Pontil: He will stand by whatever his sister decides and fears what happens if she does not decide.
sides.Corvin Hollin: He is first blower and a Hollin; he takes it as settled that it will be him.
sides.Imre Sarro: He has the better hands, and wants it on merit, not on whose son he is.
sides.Runa Sarro: She wants it for her son, and does not trust how much she wants it.
sides.Halvard Dunmore: He says aloud that Imre has the hands and Corvin the head, and that he would choose differently on different days.

situations.summary: Vessa Pontil is losing her sight and can no longer judge the colour of a melt by eye. She hides it.

sides.Vessa Pontil: Her eyes are failing. She has Lumi name the colours each morning. Ode knows; she has told nobody else.
sides.Ode Pontil: He knows his sister's eyes are failing. He has told no one.
sides.Runa Sarro: She has watched Vessa at the lehr and believes she can no longer see the colour. She has said nothing, not even to Vessa.

situations.summary: Every morning at five Lumi Pontil goes to the Cone with her grandmother Vessa and tells her what colour the melt is.

sides.Vessa Pontil: She needs Lumi's eyes and will not say why.
sides.Lumi Pontil: It is their game, before anyone else is up: she names the colour and her grandmother says whether she is right.

situations.summary: Three glasshouses have been broken since the storm: glasshouse 6 (the Greaves'), glasshouse 11 (held by the Counting House for the town) and glasshouse 13 (the Pontils'). There is glass in the lehr house for about one. Tamsin Hollin, who fits the panes, decides which is mended first.

sides.Tamsin Hollin: Whatever she chooses, two households will say she chose wrongly. The Pontils' is her husband's master's; the Greaves' is her sister's in-laws'; the town's is everyone's.
sides.Oswin Greave: Glasshouse 6 is his household's and should grow food again before anything else.
sides.Joss Tarn: If the town's glasshouse 11 is mended, he wants a share in it for the Tarns, who have none.
sides.Cora Stannard: If Oswin gets his glasshouse back, he may leave her flower corner alone; or he may not.
sides.Jory Greave: Glasshouse 6 is his family's; he also knows his tree takes a bay of the Ladder.

situations.summary: Bram Calloway has been building the Second Thought in the dry dock for four years and means to cross the Combs in it. The hull is framed. He needs fourteen trees, and only the Hanger has trees.

sides.Bram Calloway: He means to cross. He needs fourteen trees and Marit has said no.
sides.Ysolde Calloway: Her husband is building a ship to cross a reef no ship has crossed.
sides.Neve Calloway: She would sail with her father.
sides.Eamon Tarn: He wants a place on the ship and helps in the dry dock to earn it.
sides.Marit Sedge: Fourteen trees would be a fifth of the Hanger.
sides.Sabine Quill: The ship is the only thing on the island that might go past the Pale; she asks Bram about it.

situations.summary: Ysolde Calloway does not want to sail on the Second Thought. She has told Bram, at night, and not the children.

sides.Ysolde Calloway: She does not want to sail and will not say so in front of the children.
sides.Bram Calloway: Ysolde has told him she does not want to sail.

situations.summary: The Watchglass is lit every night under the keepers' vow, as it has been for eighty-three years, and burns oil rendered from fish that could have been eaten. The Counting House pays the Faros for the oil. Lark Morrow says she saw a sail beyond the Combs last spring.

sides.Anselm Faro: He swore the vow and has never missed a night.
sides.Livia Faro: She renders the oil and has begun to wonder who the light is for.
sides.Lark Morrow: She saw a sail. The light is for that.
sides.Ingrid Morrow: The lamp keeps her granddaughter's head full of ships.
sides.Aldous Quill: The ledger has paid for the oil every year for eighty-three years; it is the oldest line in the book.

situations.summary: The ledger in the Counting House holds debts in drops between households. Lorcan Vane owes the Counting House nine drops for counters losses and owes the Marver for meals and drink. The Marver owes Petra Tarn twelve drops for smoked fish since the winter.

sides.Aldous Quill: He keeps the book and writes what he is told and what is lost at counters.
sides.Lorcan Vane: He owes the Counting House and the Marver, and means to win it back.
sides.Davin Vane: His brother's debts shame the family.
sides.Petra Tarn: The Marver owes her twelve drops; Dolly says it is paid in meals.
sides.Dolly Achterberg: The Tarns have eaten off what she owes Petra; Lorcan owes her more than that.

situations.summary: Davin Vane has paid six drops of Lorcan's debt to the Marver, through Dolly Achterberg, and Aldous Quill wrote it. Lorcan does not know.

sides.Davin Vane: He has paid six drops of Lorcan's debt and not told him.
sides.Dolly Achterberg: Davin pays her quietly against his brother's debt.
sides.Aldous Quill: He wrote Davin's payments against Lorcan's debt to the Marver, as asked, without a word to Lorcan.

situations.summary: In the fever winter the Quills took twenty drops' worth of peat from the Store, and Aldous Quill wrote it in the ledger as paid. It was never paid.

sides.Aldous Quill: He wrote his own household's peat debt as paid, and hopes nobody ever checks the fever winter's page.

situations.summary: Mid Row 6 is sound, dry and unclaimed; its key hangs in the Counting House. The Tarns, seven in one house, want it. Tamsin Hollin wants it for her sister Suri Greave, who is expecting and lives with her husband's parents.

sides.Magda Tarn: Seven people in one house on Low Row; Mid Row 6 is the obvious answer.
sides.Tamsin Hollin: Her sister needs a house before the baby comes.
sides.Suri Greave: She wants a house of their own, and knows her sister is asking for this one.

situations.summary: The Kiln families have never taken a Strand apprentice at the Cone. Kit Calloway, a Strand boy, wants to blow glass. Tobiah Dunmore, a Kiln boy, stokes the Cone.

sides.Kit Calloway: He wants to blow glass and hangs about the Cone yard.
sides.Tobiah Dunmore: He stokes the Cone because his grandfather wants him at the furnace.
sides.Halvard Dunmore: No Strand boy has worked the Cone; his grandson will.
sides.Bram Calloway: His son is his apprentice and the ship needs him.
sides.Imre Sarro: His mother was born a Tarn, and he sees Kit watching him work.

situations.summary: The kelp kilns on the Wrack Strand stand upwind of Low Row, and on burning days the smoke lies along it and over the wash-house's washing.

sides.Kenji Sato: The Cone needs ash, the kilns are where the kelp is, and he is tired of hearing about it.
sides.Hana Sato: She lives in her husband's smoke and wants a house further from it.
sides.Greta Dunmore: The smoke greys the washing she keeps clean for half the town.

situations.summary: The clay bank below the Crown is nearly dug out; Otto Brandt has perhaps a season's crucibles left in it. There is good clay under the Crown, where the graves are. Nobody digs on the Crown except to bury.

sides.Otto Brandt: Without crucibles there is no glass; the only good clay left is under the graveyard.
sides.Fenn Brandt: He wants Otto to stop looking at the graveyard.
sides.Mirren Quill: She laid out most of the people buried there.
sides.Benedikt Orme: He keeps the list of the graves, and Otto has asked him where the old ones lie.

situations.summary: Imre Sarro of the Cone and Neve Calloway of the Strand love each other. Neve would sail with her father; Imre would never leave the Cone.

sides.Imre Sarro: He loves Neve and will not leave the Cone.
sides.Neve Calloway: She loves Imre and would sail.
sides.Runa Sarro: She likes Neve and sees where it leads.
sides.Bram Calloway: His daughter loves a Kiln blower.
sides.Ysolde Calloway: She would rather Neve stayed for Imre than sailed.

situations.summary: Ren Sato, a Strand fisher, is courting Sabine Quill. Her father does not approve. Sabine is not sure she does either.

sides.Ren Sato: He is courting Sabine and knows her father does not approve.
sides.Sabine Quill: Ren is kind and she likes him; she wants to know what is past the Pale more.
sides.Aldous Quill: He does not approve of a Strand fisher for his daughter.
sides.Mirren Quill: She likes Ren more than her husband does.
sides.Kenji Sato: His son is courting the tally keeper's daughter.
sides.Hana Sato: She worries the Quills look down on them.

situations.summary: Cora Stannard grows flowers in a corner of glasshouse 4. Oswin Greave, the head grower, wants the corner back for food.

sides.Cora Stannard: The flowers are hers and go to the graves.
sides.Oswin Greave: Every pane on the Ladder should grow food.

situations.summary: Jory Greave has spent three years growing a fruit tree in a bay of glasshouse 9. It has not fruited. His parents want the bay back.

sides.Elke Greave: Her son is wasting a bay on a tree.

situations.summary: The root plots need kelp carried up the hill from the Wrack Strand. The gatherers bring less than Nan Fenwick wants, because the Cone's ash wants kelp too.

sides.Nan Fenwick: She wants more kelp for the plots than she gets.
sides.Amara Okoro: She carries what she can up the wynds.
sides.Hana Sato: Her husband wants the kelp for ash.
sides.Lark Morrow: She gathers what she is told.
sides.Kenji Sato: Kelp that goes up the hill is ash the Cone does not get.

tensions.name: Fuel
tensions.made_of: Peat and wood counts in the stores; the Cone's burn rate; the size of the Hanger.

tensions.name: The succession
tensions.made_of: Vessa's failing sight (a secret, on three sheets); two blowers; no rule for who follows.

tensions.name: Panes
tensions.made_of: Three broken glasshouses; glass enough for about one; Tamsin chooses the order.

tensions.name: The ship
tensions.made_of: A hull in the dry dock; fourteen trees needed; a reef.

tensions.name: The lamp
tensions.made_of: Oil burnt each night that could be eaten or traded; a vow; a girl who saw a sail.

tensions.name: The ledger
tensions.made_of: Debts in drops between Strand and Kiln households; one false entry.

tensions.name: The empty house
tensions.made_of: Mid Row 6: sound, empty, wanted by two families. A newcomer could also ask for it.

tensions.name: Apprentices
tensions.made_of: A Strand boy who wants glass; a Kiln boy who wants the sea; a custom against both.

tensions.name: The smoke
tensions.made_of: The kelp kilns stand upwind of Low Row's washing.

tensions.name: The clay
tensions.made_of: The clay bank is nearly gone; there is more under the graveyard.

tensions.name: Two loves
tensions.made_of: Imre and Neve, across the two families; Ren and Sabine, uneven.
